title: The report gets no features for a change when the context is file-level and the repo has no surfaces
evidence: Rebuilt payload for excalidraw-11: features is empty on the clipboard changes, although feature charts-and-paste lists src/clipboard.ts in files. buildContextPack links features only through annotations and surfaces (context-pack.ts:149-152); this context has 0 annotations and 0 surfaces, and feature.files is never read. Contributing cause only: fixing it does not prove the report would then name chart paste.
possibleFixes: Link features through feature.files for the changed file, as rules already do through rule.files
pinnedBy: packages/reporting/test/known-gaps.test.ts :: GAP-002 a feature that lists the changed file is not linked to the change

title: The report describes a changed behavior as intended and does not ask what relied on the old behavior
evidence: The QA report for excalidraw-11 tells QA to verify that tabs display as eight spaces and never names spreadsheet or chart paste. The payload did hold pointers: the clipboard.ts role mentions spreadsheet data, the parseClipboard diff shows parsePotentialSpreadsheet, and charts.ts and PasteChartDialog are listed as dependents of normalizeText. One run of openai/gpt-6-luna, so variance is unknown. Follow-up on 2026-11-05 with openai/gpt-6-luna: sending receivers of the changed value, ranked and capped, with an instruction to ask what each one assumed about the old value. Without them, 0 of 2 excalidraw-11 reports mentioned spreadsheet paste. With them, 2 of 3 did, and 1 of 3 had the check that catches the bug (ordinary-pasting spreadsheet rows opens the chart flow). Report length did not grow. Improved, not closed: the report still misses it in most runs. Follow-up on 2026-11-08 with deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017, graded per check by a second model (a check counts only if it normal-pastes spreadsheet cells and expects the chart flow; plain-paste and comma-only checks do not): raw receiver list with no instruction caught it in 5 of 9 reports but explained the cause in 1 of 9; ranked receivers plus an instruction, 5 of 9 (4 explained); adding a meaning for the receiver, 9 of 10 (3 explained); a 'what did the old value guarantee' instruction, 7 of 10 (8 explained). Showing the receiver's source code made it worse: 4 of 10 reports were rejected because the model copied identifiers into its checks. A deterministic analyzer note (the receiver splits on a character the change removes) with the receiver meaning caught it in 18 of 18 valid reports (18 explained); adding the guarantees instruction also gave 18 of 18. 2 of 20 runs per setup produced no report (empty output or a rejected identifier), so 18 of 20 attempts. The note fires on 1 of 32 corpus commits (excalidraw-11) and on no other.
possibleFixes: Generalize the removed-character check beyond tab, newline, comma, semicolon and pipe, for example to number formats and case changes
Retry a report that is empty or rejected, so a failed run does not count as a miss
Repeat the run on the other consumer-type entries (7 of the 9 in the corpus) to see whether the lift holds beyond this one commit
pinExempt: LLM output is not deterministic, so a unit test cannot pin it. Track it by re-running the report on the corpus.

title: A constant built by a call with a non-function argument has no entity
evidence: The icons are `const SendBackwardIcon = createIcon(<g />)`. The collector makes entities for a call wrapping a function or an object literal, not for this form, so the change lands on the module entity. Collecting every call result would also collect ordinary values, so this was left open.
possibleFixes: Collect a call result as an entity when the callee returns a function or a component
pinnedBy: packages/analyzer/test/known-gaps.test.ts :: GAP-004 a constant built by a call with a non-function argument is not an entity

title: A value stored in an object field or shared state does not reach the code that reads it
evidence: excalidraw-07 travels through appState.activeTool, and excalidraw-09 through a rendering schedule, with no call or argument between the changed code and the code that went wrong. Following object fields as values was tested: it found nothing more on the corpus and raised the added entities from a mean of 19.7 to 28.5 per entry, and a first prototype that matched writes to reads of a field also found nothing, though it was not tuned. Neither was shipped.
possibleFixes: Field-sensitive tracking of writes to reads on the same object type
Name the state fields a change writes in the report, so the reader can check them
limitation: Changed values are followed through arguments, local variables and return values, one caller up and one call down; values stored in object fields or shared state are not followed.
pinnedBy: packages/analyzer/test/known-gaps.test.ts :: GAP-005 a value stored in a shared object field does not reach the code that reads the field
